name: Buggy Choke
description: Buggy Choke control is a bottom-side-control head-and-arm enclosure in which the bottom player connects an arm to the same-side leg and uses that loop to threaten a choke on the top player.
variant_uniqueness: Bottom player forms an arm-and-leg choke loop
summary: Buggy Choke control is a bottom-side-control head-and-arm enclosure in which the bottom player connects an arm to the same-side leg and uses that loop to threaten a choke on the top player.
overview:
The top player is beside the bottom player in side-control geometry. The bottom player has turned partly toward the opponent and brought an arm past the head. That arm connects to the same-side raised leg, enclosing the top player's head and one arm. The controlling elbow stays near the knee so the loop does not depend on wrenching the foot.

The bottom player supplies the arm-and-leg loop around the opponent's head and one arm. It does not require a collar grip, a turtle ride, or trapping the opponent's arm alone across their own throat. Terminology: Buggy choke control.

Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg. Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg. Shorten the connection through body position, not by pulling the foot hard toward the face.

Protect both the defender's neck and the attacker's knee. Do not pull the foot against a fixed knee, use a slam, or remain attached when lifted. Open the whole loop on any stop signal.

Instructional sources: [Kade and Tye Ruotolo — OG Buggy Choke](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zixbOyLpoOc); [Jay Rodriguez — three Buggy Choke mistakes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MjKERx4N4mY).
key_principles: Build the angle: Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg.
Enclose head and arm: Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg.
Keep elbow near knee: Shorten the connection through body position, not by pulling the foot hard toward the face.
Use the torso connection: Close space with the arm, leg, and torso while avoiding twisting force on your own knee.
Recover guard when space opens: Use a disengaging opponent's movement to insert frames and knees if the choke is lost.
Release if lifted: Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam.

top.name: Buggy Choke Top
top.description: Buggy Choke top perspective: Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg. Use balanced posture and safe inside frames before the loop closes.
top.overview:
The top player is responsible for recognizing and defending the control. The top player is beside the bottom player in side-control geometry. The bottom player has turned partly toward the opponent and brought an arm past the head. That arm connects to the same-side raised leg, enclosing the top player's head and one arm. The controlling elbow stays near the knee so the loop does not depend on wrenching the foot.

Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg. Use balanced posture and safe inside frames before the loop closes. Treat the choke as live even though you hold top side control.

Free the head-and-arm enclosure before changing to north-south or chasing another pin. Avoid lifting, dropping, or twisting the partner's trapped leg to force an escape. Stop before dizziness or loss of normal responsiveness; top position does not make a secured choke safe.

flashcards.question: Buggy defense: what connection should you recognize before the loop closes?
flashcards.answer: Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Arm joined to their same-side leg

plausible: Reaching arm ending at your hip
Raised leg without an arm connection
trap: Low chest frames with the leg down

flashcards.question: Buggy defense: while their hand and leg are still separate, what denies the enclosure?
flashcards.answer: Use balanced posture and safe inside frames before the loop closes.
flashcards.answer_line: Balanced posture and an inside frame

plausible: Drive your head deeper by their hip
Drift the near arm across their neck
trap: Circle north-south with a low head

flashcards.question: Buggy defense: why does holding side control not remove the choke threat?
flashcards.answer: Treat the choke as live even though you hold top side control.
flashcards.answer_line: The loop can still trap head and arm

plausible: Chest pressure separates knee/elbow
A wide base lowers their high leg
trap: A crossface removes the neck loop

flashcards.question: Buggy defense: what must be freed before changing to a north-south pin?
flashcards.answer: Free the head-and-arm enclosure before changing to north-south or chasing another pin.
flashcards.answer_line: Your head and arm from the loop

plausible: Their hand alone; head still caught
Your elbow alone; neck still caught
trap: Your hips, with the loop unchanged

flashcards.question: Buggy defense: why is lifting the bottom player a poor escape drill?
flashcards.answer: Avoid lifting, dropping, or twisting the partner's trapped leg to force an escape.
flashcards.answer_line: Fall risk with the choke attached

plausible: Lifting separates elbow from knee
Airborne hips unload the neck loop
trap: Their leg straightens before liftoff

flashcards.question: Buggy defense: what should trigger a stop even while you still occupy top position?
flashcards.answer: Stop before dizziness or loss of normal responsiveness; top position does not make a secured choke safe.
flashcards.answer_line: A secure neck loop, before symptoms

plausible: Loss of top balance after closure
Dizziness after one more adjustment
trap: No head movement after testing it

flashcards.question: Buggy defense: what bottom-player orientation appears in the reviewed side-control entry?
flashcards.answer: The top player is beside the bottom player in side-control geometry.
flashcards.answer_line: Under the pin, partly facing you

plausible: Under the pin, facing away
Flat, with no arm-to-leg connection
trap: Belly down, shoulders facing the mat

flashcards.question: Buggy defense: what supplies the loop around your upper body?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player supplies the arm-and-leg loop around the opponent's head and one arm. It does not require a collar grip, a turtle ride, or trapping the opponent's arm alone across their own throat.
flashcards.answer_line: Their connected arm and raised leg

plausible: Two hands with the leg unconnected
Two high legs without a hand grip
trap: A forearm alone; leg outside you

decision_tree.condition: When the hand-to-leg connection can be interrupted before the choke closes

Only after clearing the choke loop, when the shoulder and hip line allow a controlled change of pin

flashcards.question: Buggy attack: how should you make room to reach your raised leg from bottom side control?
flashcards.answer: Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Frame and turn partly onto your side

plausible: Stay flat and yank the foot inward
Roll belly down, leaving their head
trap: Push the chest with both arms long

flashcards.question: Buggy attack: what must your connected arm and leg actually surround?
flashcards.answer: Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg.
flashcards.answer_line: The opponent's head and one arm

plausible: Head alone, both arms outside
Wrist alone, head and shoulder free
trap: Shoulder and ribs, head outside

flashcards.question: Buggy attack: how do you shorten the connection without wrenching your own foot?
flashcards.answer: Shorten the connection through body position, not by pulling the foot hard toward the face.
flashcards.answer_line: Bring your elbow close to your knee

plausible: Pull the toes across a fixed knee
Extend your gripping arm away
trap: Flatten the torso; lift only ankle

flashcards.question: Buggy attack: which movement closes space around the opponent's neck?
flashcards.answer: Close space with the arm, leg, and torso while avoiding twisting force on your own knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Bring your shoulder toward your hip

plausible: Pull the ankle across your kneecap
Lift your head with the torso flat
trap: Extend your elbow away from the leg

flashcards.question: Buggy attack: the opponent withdraws and your loop opens; how can you recover position?
flashcards.answer: Use a disengaging opponent's movement to insert frames and knees if the choke is lost.
flashcards.answer_line: Frame and bring the knees between

plausible: Keep both arms reaching overhead
Turn your back before framing
trap: Hold the loose loop as they circle

flashcards.question: Buggy attack: what should you do when the opponent begins lifting you off the mat?
flashcards.answer: Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam.
flashcards.answer_line: Open the arm-leg loop and disengage

plausible: Tighten and hang from their neck
Pull the foot harder to limit falls
trap: Keep the grip until they kneel

flashcards.question: Buggy attack: how do you orient your torso in the reviewed bottom-side entry?
flashcards.answer: Use a partly side-on angle under the pin to shorten the arm-to-leg reach around the head and arm. Do not substitute a headfirst turn to turtle for this entry.
flashcards.answer_line: Partly toward them, under the pin

plausible: Flat, with the reaching arm extended
Belly down; their head behind you
trap: Face away beneath their chest

flashcards.question: Buggy attack: which attachment distinguishes this choke from a cross-collar choke?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player supplies the arm-and-leg loop around the opponent's head and one arm. It does not require a collar grip, a turtle ride, or trapping the opponent's arm alone across their own throat.
flashcards.answer_line: Your arm joins your own raised leg

plausible: Your hands cross in both lapels
Your forearm catches a collar tail
trap: Their sleeve loops around the neck
